enums.name: ke_result_domain
enums.doc: The domains that own a range of result codes. A domain's own codes are written `KE_RESULT_CODE(KE_RESULT_DOMAIN_ <DOMAIN >, n)` in its header, with `n` from 1 up.

enums.name: ke_result
enums.doc: What a fallible call returns: `KE_OK`, or the code of the failure. The detail of a failure goes to the failing library's log, never into the code. A caller treats a code it does not know as `KE_RESULT_GENERAL`. Ignoring the result of a call is a compiler warning where the compiler supports it.

values.name: KE_PHASE_STARTUP
values.doc: Runs once, before the other phases of the first tick.

values.name: KE_PHASE_PRE_UPDATE
values.doc: Runs once, before the other phases of the first tick.

values.name: KE_PHASE_FIXED_PRE_UPDATE
values.doc: The three fixed phases run in this order once per fixed step, as many steps as the tick's time covers, with the step's duration as `dt`.

values.name: KE_PHASE_FIXED_UPDATE
values.doc: The three fixed phases run in this order once per fixed step, as many steps as the tick's time covers, with the step's duration as `dt`.

values.name: KE_PHASE_FIXED_POST_UPDATE
values.doc: The three fixed phases run in this order once per fixed step, as many steps as the tick's time covers, with the step's duration as `dt`.

values.name: KE_PHASE_UPDATE
values.doc: The three fixed phases run in this order once per fixed step, as many steps as the tick's time covers, with the step's duration as `dt`.

values.name: KE_PHASE_POST_UPDATE
values.doc: The three fixed phases run in this order once per fixed step, as many steps as the tick's time covers, with the step's duration as `dt`.

values.name: KE_PHASE_RENDER
values.doc: Runs asynchronously against the next tick's sim phases. Its systems read extracted query results, never live storage, and may not mutate structure.

values.name: KE_PHASE_SHUTDOWN
values.doc: Runs once when the modules are unloaded, if a tick ever ran. A failure of its bodies is not reported.

structs.name: ke_vec3
structs.doc: Three floats, x then y then z.

structs.name: ke_vec4
structs.doc: Four floats, x then y then z then w.

structs.name: ke_quat
structs.doc: A rotation; the four lanes are x, y, z, w.

structs.name: ke_transform
structs.doc: Spatial transform: where a thing is, how it is turned, and how big it is.

structs.name: ke_variant_table_entry
structs.doc: One authored key and its value. Whoever accepts the key sets `consumed`; the loader reports every entry left unclaimed.

fields.name: default_value
fields.doc: What the field holds when nothing authors it. KE_VARIANT_NULL means the header declared no default and zero stands.

fields.name: enum_names
fields.doc: The names a scene may write for an integer field, in value order; a name stands for its index. NULL leaves the field numeric.

fields.name: enum_count
fields.doc: Entries in `enum_names`.

structs.name: ke_ecs_segment
structs.doc: One archetype's slice of a query match: the matched entities, plus one column base pointer per query term in the order query_register received them, each aligned 1:1 with `entities`. A tag term's column is NULL. Pointers stay valid until the next structural change.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: The entities this segment matched.

fields.name: columns
fields.doc: One base pointer per query term.

structs.name: ke_component_access
structs.doc: One component a system touches, and how. Two systems conflict when they name the same component and at least one writes it; conflicting systems never run in the same wave. A system that declares nothing conflicts with nothing, and is therefore free to run concurrently with everything.

structs.name: ke_query_decl
structs.doc: A query a system reads through: a tuple of components matched together, each with its access mode. The terms are read while register_system runs, and the runtime keeps its own copy.

fields.name: terms
fields.doc: The terms the query matches together.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Identifies the module in diagnostics.

fields.name: user_data
fields.doc: Forwarded unchanged to both hooks.

fields.name: on_load
fields.doc: Registers the module's components and systems.

fields.name: on_unload
fields.doc: Releases what the load acquired. A module that acquired nothing leaves it out.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Identifies the system in diagnostics and in the failure a body raises.

fields.name: phase
fields.doc: Which phase of the tick the body runs in.

fields.name: user_data
fields.doc: Forwarded unchanged to every call of the body.

fields.name: execute
fields.doc: The body itself.

fields.name: queries
fields.doc: Queries the system reads through; the body reads their resolved segments via ke_system_ctx_view.

fields.name: access_list
fields.doc: Cids the system touches that no query term covers, such as ordering-only tags and component access made without a query. Declaring nothing is not "no opinion" -- it says the system conflicts with nobody, so it may run concurrently with every other system in its phase. Anything touching component storage declares it here.

fields.name: per_entity
fields.doc: The body's work on one entity is independent of every other entity it visits. The runtime may then run it as several concurrent slices of the same entity set, each body call handling the share ke_system_ctx_slice reports. False keeps the body one call over the whole set. What breaks the promise is a body reaching an entity other than the one it is visiting, or touching state shared across the set.

fields.name: after
fields.doc: Names of systems of the same phase this one runs after, whatever they access. A name is resolved when the phase is built, so it may name a system registered later; a name no system of the phase carries fails the tick.

fields.name: before
fields.doc: Names of systems of the same phase this one runs before, resolved like `after`.

fields.name: exclusive
fields.doc: The body runs alone at the start of its phase, before every system of the phase that is not exclusive, and what it records is applied before they run. Two exclusive systems are ordered like two writers of one component. Neither its access nor per_entity orders or splits it.

fields.name: fixed_dt
fields.doc: Timestep KE_PHASE_FIXED_UPDATE runs at, in seconds. 0 selects 1/60.

fields.name: fixed_dt_max_accum
fields.doc: Largest catch-up budget a tick may accumulate, in seconds; excess is discarded. 0 selects 0.25.

fields.name: max_systems_per_phase
fields.doc: Most systems one phase may hold; registering past it fails. 0 selects 256.

slots.name: entity_create
slots.doc: Creates a fresh entity with no components. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

params.name: out_entity
params.doc: Receives the entity; the null entity on failure.

slots.name: entity_destroy
slots.doc: Destroys an entity and all its components; an entity that is not alive is left alone. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for the null entity or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

slots.name: component_register
slots.doc: Registers a component type by name, or returns the existing id if already registered. A repeated name must describe the same size, alignment and layout as its first registration. With `fields` the layouts are compared field by field; without them, only the size and the alignment are compared.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT when the params are missing, the alignment is not a power of two, or the type conflicts with the name's prior registration, what disagrees being logged; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: params
params.doc: The name, size, alignment and field table of the type.

params.name: out_cid
params.doc: Receives the component's id; KE_COMPONENT_INVALID on failure.

slots.name: component_lookup
slots.doc: Looks up a previously registered component by name.
slots.return_doc: false if no component of that name is registered.

params.name: name
params.doc: Component name to find.

params.name: out_meta
params.doc: Receives the component's id, size, and field metadata.

slots.name: component_add
slots.doc: Attaches a component to an entity: its storage is zeroed, then seeded with the defaults of the field table the component was registered with, on the first attach; an entity that already has the component keeps its storage unchanged. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an entity that is not alive, the null entity or component, or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

params.name: out_data
params.doc: Receives the storage, valid until the next structural change on this ecs; NULL for a tag, and on failure.

slots.name: component_remove
slots.doc: Detaches a component from an entity; an entity that is not alive is left alone. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for the null entity or component, or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

slots.name: component_get
slots.doc: Returns an entity's component storage, or NULL if it doesn't have that component. The pointer is valid until the next structural change on this ecs.

slots.name: component_size
slots.doc: Byte size of a registered component's element; 0 for a tag or unknown cid.

slots.name: component_field_write
slots.doc: Writes value into component at the place field describes, converted to the field's type: an integer and a float convert to each other, a boolean to an integer, and a vector widens or narrows to the field's width; a string is cut to the field's size and stays NUL-terminated.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a null argument, or for a value that does not convert to the field's type or a size the type cannot have, writing nothing.

params.name: component
params.doc: The component's memory.

params.name: field
params.doc: Where in the component, and of which type and size.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to write.

slots.name: query_register
slots.doc: Registers a query over a component tuple (entities matching ALL cids).
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an empty tuple, one with more terms than the backend's queries hold, or one the backend refuses, its reason logged; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: cids
params.doc: Component tuple to match.

params.name: cid_count
params.doc: Number of components in the tuple.

params.name: out_query
params.doc: Receives the query; KE_QUERY_INVALID on failure.

slots.name: query_resolve
slots.doc: Resolves a query into archetype segments. MUST run single-threaded, before a parallel wave; afterwards the segments are plain memory touching no backend state.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an unknown query, missing output arrays or a zero capacity, or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

params.name: out_segments
params.doc: Receives the matched segments.

params.name: max_segments
params.doc: Capacity of out_segments.

params.name: out_columns
params.doc: Backing store of the segments' columns: segment i's columns are the cid_count entries starting at index i * cid_count, cid_count being the length of the tuple the query was registered with.

params.name: out_count
params.doc: Receives how many segments the query matches; above max_segments, out_segments holds only the first max_segments of them; zero on failure.

slots.name: entity_reserve
slots.doc: Reserves an entity id, callable concurrently from any wave thread — the one entity operation that is. The id is usable immediately as a reference; the entity itself appears in the world when component_add first runs for it, at the wave barrier. An implementation may not satisfy this by forwarding to entity_create, which is single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY when every id the implementation can reserve was handed out.

params.name: out_entity
params.doc: Receives the id; the null entity on failure.

slots.name: entity_materialize
slots.doc: Brings a reserved id into the world, so an entity that never receives a component still exists. Structural; single-threaded. A no-op for an id that is already alive or was never reserved.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for the null entity or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

vtables.name: ke_runtime
vtables.doc: Owns the simulation world, dispatches systems across the worker pool and drives the frame loop.

slots.name: register_module
slots.doc: Loads a module into the runtime, running its load hook before returning.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK, the code the load hook failed with, or KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: p
params.doc: What the module is called and the hooks it registers.

params.name: out_id
params.doc: Receives the module's id; 0 on failure.

slots.name: register_system
slots.doc: Registers a system body against the phase and the component access it declares. Registered from a body, the system takes effect with the next tick and a refusal is not reported.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a body, phase or declaration the runtime refuses; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY when the phase is full or storage cannot grow.

params.name: p
params.doc: What the system is called, when it runs, and what it touches.

params.name: out_id
params.doc: Receives the system's id; 0 on failure.

slots.name: unregister_system
slots.doc: Removes a system registered earlier. Called from a body, the removal takes effect with the next tick.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK, or KE_RESULT_NOT_FOUND when no system has that id.

slots.name: last_system
slots.doc: The id of the system registered last and still registered, or 0 when there is none.

slots.name: declare_exclusive
slots.doc: Declares member one of the members of the exclusive group group: no entity holds two members of one group. Two systems whose every query requires a different member of the same group touch disjoint entities, so what they access through their queries puts no order between them; what their access lists name still does.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK, KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT when group equals member, or KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY when the declaration cannot be stored.

slots.name: declare_self_ordered
slots.doc: Declares that whoever owns cid orders the systems writing it, so the runtime puts no order between two writers of cid. A writer still runs before a system that only reads it.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK, or KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY when the declaration cannot be stored.

slots.name: check_order
slots.doc: Builds the order of every phase as the next tick would. Within a phase, a system runs after the systems it names in `after` and before those it names in `before`, a writer of a component before a system that only reads it, and of two writers with neither order, the one registered first runs first: an ambiguity.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_NOT_FOUND when an `after` or a `before` names no system of its phase; KE_RESULT_GENERAL when the order has a cycle or, when refused, two writers are ambiguous. The systems involved are named in the log.

params.name: refuse_ambiguity
params.doc: When true, an ambiguity fails the check too.

slots.name: tick
slots.doc: Runs one tick: every sim phase in order, then the render phase. This is where a body that failed during the tick is answered for.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK, or the code a body of this tick failed with.

slots.name: flush_render
slots.doc: Blocks until any render phase dispatched by a previous tick() has finished, and fails with whatever a body of that phase failed with. That phase outlives the tick that dispatched it, so this is where its failure is reported rather than by the tick that started it. tick() dispatches render asynchronously and returns before it completes; callers that need to tear down render-owned native resources must call this first, or the still-running render phase races the teardown. A no-op if nothing is pending.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK, or the code a body of the render phase failed with.

slots.name: unload_modules
slots.doc: Waits for any pending render phase, runs the shutdown phase if a tick ever ran, then calls every module's unload hook in the reverse of registration order. The host calls it while everything a module's unload hook uses is still alive; destroying the runtime calls it for a host that did not. A second call does nothing.

vtables.name: ke_ecs_commands
vtables.doc: A queue of structural mutations. Every operation records its intent and returns; none changes the world while it runs. The queue is applied, in the order the operations were recorded, by whoever owns it, and an operation's effect is not observable before then. A caller needing a change visible at once uses ke_ecs, which mutates immediately. Recording never touches the world, so these operations may be called while other code reads it. The queue is applied while nothing else runs. An implementation that cannot accept an operation returns its code, logs the reason, and leaves the queue unchanged: KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED in a phase that may not change structure, KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY when the queue cannot grow.

slots.name: spawn
slots.doc: Records the creation of an entity and answers the id it will have. The id can be named by later operations of this queue, and by any caller, at once; the entity itself exists once the queue is applied.

params.name: out_entity
params.doc: Receives the id; KE_ENTITY_INVALID on failure.

slots.name: attach
slots.doc: Records giving `entity` the component `cid`, initialised from `size` bytes of `data`. The bytes are copied, so the caller's buffer need not outlive the call. `size` must equal the registered size of `cid`, or be 0 to attach the component without copying bytes into it.
slots.return_doc: KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT, besides the codes above, when `size` is neither 0 nor the registered size of `cid`.

slots.name: detach
slots.doc: Records removing component `cid` from `entity`.

slots.name: despawn
slots.doc: Records destroying `entity`.

slots.name: defer
slots.doc: Records a structural operation for work the fixed verbs above cannot express. `fn` runs when the queue is applied, in order with the other operations. `user_size` bytes of `user` are copied, so the caller's buffer need not outlive the call.
slots.return_doc: KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT, besides the codes above, for a null `fn`.

vtables.name: ke_system_ctx
vtables.doc: What one call of a system body is given to work with: the entities its queries resolved to, which share of them it owns, and the queue it records structural changes into. It exists for the duration of the call and means nothing outside it. `handle` is runtime-private.

fields.name: commands
fields.doc: The queue this body records structural changes into, applied at the wave barrier. In the render phase the queue refuses every operation.

slots.name: view
slots.doc: The system body's only path to component memory. Returns the resolved archetype segments for the system's query at query_index (the order the queries were declared in ke_runtime_system_params). Sets *out_count to the segment count and returns the segment array; both are valid for the duration of the system body. Makes no ke_ecs call. Returns NULL for an out-of-range index or a system that declared no queries.

slots.name: slice
slots.doc: Reports which share of its entity set this body call owns: *out_index in [0, *out_count). A system that did not declare per_entity always gets index 0 of count 1.

vtables.name: ke_task_pool
vtables.doc: Dispatches work to a native thread pool.

slots.name: dispatch
slots.doc: Schedules a task, which the caller releases by waiting on it.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK, KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a null func or out_task, KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY, or KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED when the pool does not accept the calling thread.

params.name: func
params.doc: Entry point invoked on a worker thread.

params.name: data
params.doc: Opaque context passed to func unchanged.

params.name: out_task
params.doc: Receives the task; null on failure.

slots.name: dispatch_on_complete
slots.doc: Schedules a task and a completion callback run once it finishes.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK, KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a null func or out_task, KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY, or KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED when the pool does not accept the calling thread.

params.name: func
params.doc: Entry point invoked on a worker thread.

params.name: data
params.doc: Opaque context passed to func unchanged.

params.name: on_complete
params.doc: Invoked after func returns.

params.name: user_data
params.doc: Opaque context passed to on_complete unchanged.

params.name: out_task
params.doc: Receives the task; null on failure.

slots.name: wait
slots.doc: Blocks the calling thread until the task completes, releases the task, and returns what its body returned. Every task a dispatch slot returns is waited on exactly once: afterwards the pointer is invalid for wait and is_completed alike, and a task never waited on is never released and reports its failure nowhere.
slots.return_doc: What the task body returned, or KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a null task.

slots.name: is_completed
slots.doc: Returns true if the task has finished. Valid only before the task is waited on.

slots.name: get_num_workers
slots.doc: Returns the number of worker threads in the pool.

functions.name: ke_runtime_create
functions.doc: Creates a runtime over ecs and task_pool, both borrowed for its lifetime.
functions.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a null ecs, task_pool or out_runtime; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: params
params.doc: NULL takes every default.

params.name: out_runtime
params.doc: Receives the runtime; left zeroed on failure.

callbacks.name: ke_module_load_fn
callbacks.doc: Registers the module's components and systems against the runtime it is being loaded into. Runs inside register_module, before that call returns.

lanes.name: runtime
lanes.doc: The runtime the module is being loaded into.

callbacks.name: ke_module_unload_fn
callbacks.doc: Releases whatever the matching load acquired, as the modules are unloaded.

lanes.name: runtime
lanes.doc: The runtime the module was loaded into.

callbacks.name: ke_system_execute_fn
callbacks.doc: One call of a system body. The runtime calls it once per tick the system's phase runs, or once per slice when the system declared per_entity. A body runs on a worker thread; the code it returns is carried to the thread driving the tick, which tick() then fails with, and the runtime logs the system's name. The remaining bodies of the same wave still run — they were already dispatched — but no later phase of that tick starts.

lanes.name: ctx
lanes.doc: The body's only doorway to component memory for this call. Opaque; pass it to the entry points that take one.

lanes.name: dt
lanes.doc: Seconds since the previous tick, or the fixed timestep in the three fixed phases.

callbacks.name: ke_defer_fn
callbacks.doc: A structural operation applied when the queue holding it is drained. `user` points at the copy of the payload passed to defer; `ecs` is the live world. A failure is returned, and the queue stops there: the operations recorded after it are dropped.

callbacks.name: ke_task_func
callbacks.doc: Body of a scheduled task, run on a worker thread.

lanes.name: data
lanes.doc: Opaque context handed to the dispatch call.

callbacks.name: ke_task_on_complete_func
callbacks.doc: Run once the task body has returned, on the same worker thread.

lanes.name: user_data
lanes.doc: Opaque context handed to the dispatch call.
